explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. The LORD tells Moses to say, "…if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD…" (Numbers 6:2). Nobody needs a title, a tribe or a fancy hat for this one. I own a very tall hat and it still doesn't count for anything here.

Ooh, nice guess, but the door is WIDER than that, friend. The LORD says, "…if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite…" (Numbers 6:2). Nothing in that verse says only priests can sign up. The priest does show up later to handle the offerings. He's more like the guy running the oven than the only one allowed to bake.

Nope, no leader requirement anywhere in the verse. The LORD says "…if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD…" (Numbers 6:2). A man or a woman, that's the whole guest list. Nobody has to be in charge of anything to sign up.

Not quite, friend. It sounds sneaky-smart, but the text says he "…must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins." (Numbers 6:3). Verse 4 goes further: nothing from the grapevine, "…not even the seeds or skins." So the raisin cookie is off the menu for him, and I feel for him on that one.

Right, it's False! Wine isn't the only thing on the list. The text says he "…must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins." (Numbers 6:3). Then it adds that he's not to eat anything from the grapevine, "…not even the seeds or skins." (Numbers 6:4). The LORD covers the whole vine, top to bottom.

Yes, friend! For the entire period of his vow, "…no razor shall touch his head." (Numbers 6:5). The text says he "…must let the hair of his head grow long." That's the whole vow, start to finish. I'd say that razor is going to sit in a drawer feeling real left out.

Good thought, but a comb isn't what the text names. It says "…no razor shall touch his head." (Numbers 6:5). The hair is to grow long for the whole vow. So the razor is the thing that stays far, far away.

A crown sounds fancy, I'll give you that! But the text says "…no razor shall touch his head." (Numbers 6:5). Nobody is putting on anything here. The hair is simply left alone to grow long for the whole vow.

Not quite, friend, and I think this one is a heavy line to read. The text says, "Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself…" (Numbers 6:7). There's no "just this once." Verse 7 gives the reason: the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head.

Right, it's False. I think this is one of the hardest lines in the passage. The text says, "Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself…" (Numbers 6:7). No exception is given for family. The reason is that the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head.

explanations.answer: His head carries the sign of his vow to God
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker! The text says, "…because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head." (Numbers 6:7). That's the reason it gives, even when the dead is family. His head carries the sign of his vow, so the LORD's "stay away" holds.

explanations.answer: His hands carry the offerings for the altar
explanations.explanation: Good try, but hands and offerings aren't the reason given. The text says the Nazirite stays away "…because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head." (Numbers 6:7). It's about his head. Hands are busy enough at my place without adding to the story.

explanations.answer: His robe carries the mark of his tribe
explanations.explanation: I like the creativity, but there's no robe or tribe mark in this verse. The reason is "…because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head." (Numbers 6:7). It's all about the head, friend. Keep your eye on the head.

Yes, friend! If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated hair, "…he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing…" (Numbers 6:9). That's the seventh day. All that growing, and the hair has to come off anyway. I think that one hurts.

Washing clothes is a sensible guess, but this passage never mentions it here. The text says he "…must shave his head on the day of his cleansing…" (Numbers 6:9). The defiled thing is his consecrated hair, so the hair is what goes. The laundry can wait.

Oil is a nice thought, but this passage doesn't mention oil for this moment. The text says he "…must shave his head on the day of his cleansing…" (Numbers 6:9). That's the seventh day. Consecrating his head again comes up in verse 11: "On that day he must consecrate his head again." (Numbers 6:11). So the hair is what the cleansing day is about.

Seventh it is, baker! If someone suddenly dies in his presence, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing, the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). Then the eighth day brings the birds for the priest (Numbers 6:10). Seven days of waiting while that hair sits there defiled. I think I'd be checking the mirror every morning.
Third is a solid guess, but it's not the day the text gives. The day of cleansing is the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). The birds come on the eighth day (Numbers 6:10). Day three doesn't get a mention.

Tenth runs a bit late, friend. The text gives the day of cleansing as the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). The birds come on the eighth day (Numbers 6:10). That puts the tenth day after both. Count again and you'll land it.

True, and well done! The priest offers one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and then the text says, "On that day he must consecrate his head again." (Numbers 6:11). A fresh start for his head. The vow starts over, too.

Not quite, friend. It's True. After the priest offers the two birds, the text says, "On that day he must consecrate his head again." (Numbers 6:11). So he does rededicate it, and he doesn't skip that step.

That's right, baker! The text says, "But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled." (Numbers 6:12). He rededicates his time of separation to the LORD and starts over. It's like a whole batch of dough dumped on the floor and the timer set back to zero.

explanations.answer: They count toward the new vow
explanations.explanation: Nice hope, but it doesn't go that way. The text says, "But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled." (Numbers 6:12). He must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD. The days before don't carry over, so the count starts again.

Half credit sounds generous, friend, but the text doesn't say it. It says, "But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled." (Numbers 6:12). None of them count. The new time of separation starts from the beginning.

That's right. The Nazirite is "…to shave his consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering." (Numbers 6:18). So the long hair ends up on the fire, under the offering. After all that growing, that's quite the finish.

The basket is in this passage, so I see the pull! But it holds "…unleavened cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil…" (Numbers 6:15). The hair goes "…on the fire under the peace offering." (Numbers 6:18). The text sends it to the fire, not the basket.

Good thought, since that's where hair usually lands. But the text says he is to "…take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering." (Numbers 6:18). It doesn't go on the ground. It goes into the fire.

The priest, yes! After the wave before the LORD, the text says, "This is a holy portion for the priest…" (Numbers 6:20). That's in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the thigh that was presented. I think that priest is walking out with a full cookie box and zero complaints. You read that one right, baker!

Good thought, since the priest does put those items into the Nazirite's hands first (Numbers 6:19). But after the wave, the text says, "This is a holy portion for the priest…" (Numbers 6:20). So they end up as the priest's portion. The Nazirite gets to hold them, but not keep them.

The Levites are a fair guess, but they aren't mentioned in this passage. After the wave offering, the text says, "This is a holy portion for the priest…" (Numbers 6:20). It's the priest's portion, along with the breast and the thigh. Keep your eye on the priest.

True, baker! The text says, "After that, the Nazirite may drink wine." (Numbers 6:20). That comes after the shave and the wave offering. The time of separation is complete (Numbers 6:13). Patience paid off, friend.
Not quite, friend. It's True. After the shave and the wave offering, the text says, "After that, the Nazirite may drink wine." (Numbers 6:20). The vow is finished, so the rule for it is finished too.

That's it, baker! The text says, "he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation." (Numbers 6:21). If you make the promise, you keep it. It's as simple as saying you'll bring the cookies and then actually bringing the cookies.

Tempting when the days get long, I know! But the text says, "he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation." (Numbers 6:21). It doesn't mention shortening it. The word it uses is fulfill, so the vow is his to carry through.

Nice try, but the vow isn't something he hands over. The text says, "he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation." (Numbers 6:21). The priest helps with the offerings, but the vow belongs to the Nazirite. He's the one who has to see it through.
